title: Dialogue: buying mangoes
description: Follow and take part in a complete bargaining conversation at a fruit stall, with prices, quantities and change.

guide.title: The situation
guide.text:
You are at a fruit stall in a Kolkata market in May, when the mangoes come in. The phrases of this unit are the lines of the conversation in order; the notes say who is speaking.

Customer and stallholder call each other আপনি, and you address him as দাদা. The tone is brisk and good-humoured: bargaining is a game both sides enjoy, and nobody is offended by a low offer.

The arithmetic: he asks 100 a kilo, you offer 80, you settle on 90; two kilos come to 180; you pay with 200 and get 20 back.

guide.title: Things to notice
guide.text:
আমের দাম - 'the price of mangoes': আম + the possessive -এর.

একশো টাকা কিলো - 'a hundred rupees a kilo'. No word for 'per' is needed.

খেয়ে দেখুন - 'eat and see': the -e form + দেখা means 'try doing'. In the same way পরে দেখুন, 'try it on'; বলে দেখুন, 'try asking'.

না হলে - 'if it is not (so)': the -le form of হওয়া with না before it. ফেরত দেবেন, 'you will give back'.

আশি টাকায় - 'for eighty rupees': the price you buy AT takes the 'at' ending. আশিতে হবে না - 'at eighty it won't do'.

হবে না is the all-purpose refusal: 'no can do'.

এই থাক - 'let this stay', that is, 'that will be all'. থাক is the 'let it' form of থাকা.

এই নিন - 'here, take': said when handing something over.
